# Context

The ANOVA of the durum wheat trial (`loc07_year1`, 24 genotypes, 4 blocks) says that **at least one genotype is different**. It does not say which. WAHA is a widely grown variety.

**The breeder's question:** is any genotype better than WAHA, and by how much?

Four procedures answer different questions: **LSD** controls nothing (5% in every pair), **Duncan** is in between but has no control of the error of all comparisons, **Tukey** controls the error of all pairs together, and **Dunnett** controls the error of the comparisons with one control.

```{r packages}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(agricolae)
library(emmeans)
```

```{r data}
durum <- read.csv("data/Durum_wheat_Algeria.csv")
e7 <- durum %>%
  filter(Environment == "loc07_year1") %>%
  mutate(Genotype = relevel(factor(Genotype), ref = "WAHA"),   # WAHA is the control
         Block = factor(Block))

fit <- lm(yield ~ Block + Genotype, data = e7)
c(MSE = deviance(fit) / df.residual(fit), df = df.residual(fit))
```

# LSD

```{r lsd}
lsd <- LSD.test(fit, "Genotype", console = FALSE)
lsd$statistics$LSD       # about 0.20 t/ha
lsd$groups               # same letter = not significantly different
```

The LSD is `t x SED`. Check it by hand:

```{r lsd-hand}
mse <- deviance(fit) / df.residual(fit)
r <- 4                                  # replicates (blocks)
sed <- sqrt(2 * mse / r)

# HINT: the t value uses the error degrees of freedom of the model (df.residual(fit))
qt(0.975, ___) * sed                    # TODO: should match lsd$statistics$LSD
2 * sed                                 # the approximation LSD = 2 x SED
```

**Your findings:** how many different letters (groups) does the LSD give? Is `2 x SED` close to the exact LSD? _...write here..._

# Tukey

```{r tukey}
# HINT: the same call as LSD.test, with HSD.test
tk <- HSD.test(fit, "___", console = FALSE)    # TODO: the factor to compare is Genotype
tk$statistics$MSD        # minimum significant difference, about 0.38 t/ha
tk$groups
```

**Your findings:** why is the Tukey difference larger than the LSD? How many groups now? _...write here..._

# Duncan

```{r duncan}
dn <- duncan.test(fit, "Genotype", console = FALSE)
dn$groups
```

**Your findings:** is the number of groups between LSD and Tukey? Duncan is common in papers, but it does not control the error of all comparisons: read its letters as screening. _...write here..._

# The three procedures side by side

```{r side-by-side}
n_groups <- function(x) length(unique(x$groups$groups))
data.frame(procedure = c("LSD", "Duncan", "Tukey"),
           groups = c(n_groups(lsd), n_groups(dn), n_groups(tk)),
           min_difference = c(lsd$statistics$LSD, NA, tk$statistics$MSD))
# You should get 12, 9 and 3 groups
```

```{r pairs}
em <- emmeans(fit, ~ Genotype)
n_pairs <- nrow(as.data.frame(pairs(em)))            # 24 genotypes: 276 pairs
c(pairs = n_pairs,
  unadjusted = sum(as.data.frame(pairs(em, adjust = "none"))$p.value < 0.05),
  tukey      = sum(as.data.frame(pairs(em, adjust = "tukey"))$p.value < 0.05))
```

**Your findings:** how many pairs are called different without protection and with Tukey? With 276 pairs and no real differences, how many false positives would we expect at 5%? _...write here..._

# Dunnett: genotypes against WAHA

```{r dunnett}
# HINT: WAHA is the first level of Genotype (we put it first with relevel)
dun <- summary(contrast(em, method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = ___), infer = TRUE)    # TODO
dun %>% select(contrast, estimate, SE, lower.CL, upper.CL, p.value) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r protected}
unadj <- summary(contrast(em, "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 1), adjust = "none")
c(unadjusted = sum(unadj$p.value < 0.05), dunnett = sum(dun$p.value < 0.05))
# You should get 8 without protection and 3 with Dunnett
```

```{r dunnett-plot}
dun %>% mutate(contrast = reorder(contrast, estimate)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(estimate, contrast)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower.CL, xmax = upper.CL)) +
  labs(x = "Difference to WAHA (t/ha)", y = NULL)
```

**Your findings:** which genotypes are higher than WAHA, once the 23 comparisons are protected? How many would the unprotected tests have declared? _...write here..._

# Statistical and practical significance

A difference can be significant and still too small to matter. Express the best genotype as a percentage of WAHA:

```{r percent}
mean_waha <- mean(e7$yield[e7$Genotype == "WAHA"])

best <- dun %>% slice_max(estimate, n = 1)
best$contrast

# HINT: percentage = 100 x difference / mean of WAHA (the same for the limits of the interval)
100 * c(estimate = best$estimate, lower = best$lower.CL, upper = best$upper.CL) / ___    # TODO
# You should get about 45% (interval about 12% to 77%)
```

**Your findings:** by what percentage is the best genotype above WAHA? Does the interval stay above 10%? What would the breeder decide? _...write here..._

# Extra: comparing means after a transformation

In Exercise 5 the larvae counts needed a square root. The comparison is done on the transformed scale and then reported in the original units. T9 is the untreated control:

```{r larvae}
library(agridat)
data(gomez.nonnormal1)
larv <- gomez.nonnormal1
f_sqrt <- lm(sqrt(larvae + 0.5) ~ rep + trt, data = larv)

em_l <- emmeans(f_sqrt, ~ trt)
summary(contrast(em_l, "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = 9), infer = TRUE) %>%
  select(contrast, estimate, lower.CL, upper.CL, p.value)
# Only one treatment (T7) is clearly different from the control
```

**Your findings:** which insecticides reduce the larvae compared with the control, with the protection of Dunnett? The estimates are on the square-root scale; what does that mean for the interpretation? _...write here..._
